decisions.reason: As a recently launched line close to the core door-hardware business, it is likely to be retained because the firm has already invested in multiple models and there is no clear evidence yet that poor results are permanent.
This handle family fits the established portfolio and broad-range strategy, so management is likely to continue with it rather than admit an early mistake after launch.

As a single design close to the existing offer and with less visible strategic commitment than a system family, it is somewhat easier to remove, but after only a short time management would still tend to keep it.

This product appears to require less commitment than a larger family or system, yet its proximity to the firm’s established business and the absence of decisive failure signals make continued market presence more likely.
Because it is a multi-model family within the firm’s core architectural hardware range, sunk development and launch effort support keeping it on the market for longer.

As a flagship electronic access system publicly presented as part of the firm’s future direction, management is very unlikely to withdraw it quickly because investment, visibility and justification pressures are all high.
